test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 9 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In a certain code language, 'BLISS' is written as 'KSNVT' and 'LIGHT' is written as 'UPLKU'. How will 'WHITE' be written in that language?
solution:
The alphabets and its positional values are:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26d6744000c534bf451c1971808a438dd123f54abcc92aa982430e4ce5f353c2.png] 

The logic followed here is shown below:

'BLISS' is written as 'KSNVT' 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18f4eb4dd6de98dea0effc5b08c9dc7b01930c28254d56796e9b97f38fac460d.png] 

And 

'LIGHT' is written as 'UPLKU'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1bd7403d1c5990faee289f90e17fff29eeb7ef3aa37bc255c0f428037a669c0b.png] 

Similarly,

'WHITE' will be written as **'FONWF'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/093cdf34b11981484829091b4cfc6b082c863d0c908b615dad4a8a87137714d4.png] 

Hence, the code language for 'WHITE' is '**FONWF**'.
